newsitem.title: UK: HEDGE FUND BUYER PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON GOVETT ORIENTAL.
newsitem.headline: HEDGE FUND BUYER PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON GOVETT ORIENTAL.

text.p: Govett Oriental Investment Trust said on Thursday U.S. arbitrageur Sierra Trading and affiliates had taken a 10 percent position in the trust.
Sierra Trading purchased the position, worth about 65 million sterling, from SBC Warburg.
Govett Oriental shares rose to 188 pence on the news -- a 52-week high -- and up from 177 pence earlier in the week.
But this is still a substantial discount to the trust's 208.53 pence per share net asset value (NAV).
"With a holding of ten percent he must be meaning to try and force some change in the structure of the trust," said Simon Colson, an analyst at NatWest Securities.
Sierra Trading manager Andrew Shechtel, who has purchased some Govett Oriental shares on his own account, declined to comment late Wednesday on his firm's intentions.
Sierra Trading has a reputation for building up positions in undervalued investment trusts in order to force a change in structure.
After Sierra built up a nine percent stake in American Trust earlier this year, manager Edinburgh Fund Managers elected to convert the trust to a tracker fund and halve its annual management fee.
Govett officials declined to comment but analysts believe that it is likely to put up a fight if pressured to liquidate the fund.
"This is an important investment trust for Govett and they are likely to defend it robustly," Colson said.
Govett Oriental, at 650 million sterling, represent a sizeable share of John Govett & Co's $5.5 billion under management.
Analyst Graeme Caton of Sutherlands Limited defended Govett Oriental's performance, saying it had fared relatively well in a sector that has been difficult in recent months.
But the fund's broad focus -- it invests in both developing Pacific rim nations and Japan -- may have led to the steep discount to NAV and made it a target.
"People say: Why not just invest in a top-ten Japan fund and a top-ten Far East fund?" said an analyst who asked not to be named.
